analyzed_vuln.description: `gen_literal_array()` misaccounts interpolation results in `%I`/`%W` literal arrays. In the `NODE_BEGIN` path it calls `codegen(..., VAL)` and then unconditionally increments the local component count `j`, even though malformed/error-recovered or value-less interpolation ASTs are not guaranteed to push a register value. `j` can therefore exceed the actual VM stack depth. The subsequent `while (j >= 2)` performs two compiler-stack pops and emits `OP_STRCAT` for a register below the current word. For `%I`, that register may hold a previously completed word already converted to an immediate Symbol by `OP_INTERN`, or stale data. At runtime `mrb_vm_exec()` passes this non-string as the destination to `mrb_str_concat`; `mrb_str_cat` converts it with `mrb_str_ptr` and `mrb_check_frozen` dereferences the resulting wild pointer, causing the reported SEGV.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer copies attacker bytes into a NUL-terminated buffer and passes them to `mrb_load_string`. The input must parse, including through parser error recovery, into an interpolated word/symbol literal (`%W` or, as in this PoV, `%I`) containing a `NODE_BEGIN` interpolation whose generated expression leaves no value despite being requested with `VAL`, followed by another string/interpolation component that makes `j >= 2`. A prior completed `%I` word makes the underflowed destination register contain an interned Symbol. Executing the emitted `OP_STRCAT` then treats that Symbol/stale register as a mutable `RString` and crashes.

args: Analyze the stack-accounting root cause and best minimal fix for gen_literal_array() at mruby/mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/codegen.c:1267. In particular, should its NODE_BEGIN case compare cursp() before/after codegen(..., VAL), and if no value was produced should it skip the component or emit an empty string/nil? Are there upstream mruby fixes or analogous interpolation stack-accounting patterns in this codebase?

The supplied ASan report says malformed/error-recovered %I/%W interpolation can contain a NODE_BEGIN whose codegen(..., VAL) leaves no register value. gen_literal_array currently increments local j unconditionally, then while (j >= 2) pops twice and emits OP_STRCAT below the actual stack, possibly concatenating into an interned Symbol from a previous %I word. I inspected mruby/mrbgems/mruby-compiler/core/codegen.c:1267-1317 and confirmed NODE_STR and NODE_BEGIN share codegen(..., VAL); ++j. codegen's NODE_BEGIN implementation at lines 1446-1455 only guarantees nil for a genuinely empty list, and malformed AST/control-flow nodes can apparently leave no value despite VAL. We need a root-cause C-source patch preserving valid interpolation behavior, likely deriving j from actual compiler stack movement rather than assumed movement.
